items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: he played with John Robeshow when he was down in that pit.

ctx.x: He wasn't playing with the reading bands much then, huh?
Well, yeah, he played with John Robeshow when he was down in that pit. Uh-huh. And he had to read the state on that pit.
And he played some jazz too at the same, on the same job? Yeah. Yeah. With Robeshow? Yeah.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: Old man John Robichaud, he had a band at the Lyrics Theatre.

ctx.x: We would have played the second. We had a nice band over there at the lights.

They had the lyrics theater that time. It was right on the corner. We had a nice band over there at the lights. And they had all those ministries coming in venison stuff come over there after the show, between shows, and the show was out around 11, 30, 12 o'clock at night, unless we was giving a midnight ramble. We had a lot of musicians used to come in there from off, out of town musicians used to build the shows, come in, stop there, listen, a lot of them used to come in and sit in. Old man John Robichaud, he…
I never knew him, but I heard a lot of guys talk about him.
Did you say P-Ron would play for a special class of people though, huh?

Yeah, he played for the better class of people, see. He played for the doctors and the lawyers and people up here on St. Charles Street, people back in the place and all that kind of people, the higher class of people, see. And they liked that sweet music and slow and waltzes a lot of things, you know, something like that. Well, the average band around here didn't play that, see. Like John Robeshoe and P-Ron. And they had another fellow here called Peter Bocard and his bunch. Now they played all that kind of…
He had a good band. I had a good band.
